subject: Taxes
title: The Peasants' Revolt of 1381
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Peasants' Revolt of 1381.

hook.text: In 1381, English peasants marched on London and beheaded the Archbishop of Canterbury.

buildup.text: The Black Death had killed a third of England. Survivors demanded higher wages, but nobles froze pay and piled on taxes.

discovery.text: Wat Tyler led 60,000 rebels into London. They burned tax records and opened prisons. The king met them at Mile End.

twist.text: Tyler was killed during negotiations, and the revolt collapsed. But the poll tax was never collected again.

climax.text: The revolt failed in its moment but succeeded in its legacy. England abandoned poll taxes for over 600 years.

punchline.text: 60,000 rebels, one dead archbishop. The poll tax died with them.

quiz.question: What triggered England's Peasants' Revolt of 1381?
